cues: Farm crews cut heavy bunches while still green, then carry them carefully to washing and packing lines.
Ripening rooms meter ethylene gas to turn shipped green fruit yellow on a closely monitored schedule.
Home cooks freeze peeled pieces on trays, then blend them into thick, dairy-free soft serve.
Growers remove the spent flower stalk after fruiting, while new shoots emerge near the plant’s base.
Street vendors slice the fruit lengthwise, fry it in hot oil, and serve it as a savory side.
Cooks coat peeled fruit in chocolate, freeze it on sticks, and serve it as a chilled treat.
